file_verdicts.summary: Prebuilt binaries from GitHub; checksums present; no malicious code

audits.body:
Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/agentty-bin.git...
Cloned agentty-bin
Analyzing agentty-bin AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines sources for two architectures (x86_64 and aarch64) that point directly to prebuilt binary releases from the project's GitHub repository under `https://github.com/1ay1/agentty`. The URLs are constructed using tagged release versions (`v${pkgver}`), which is standard practice for `-bin` packages. The `sha256sums` are present and non-SKIP, meaning the integrity of the downloaded binaries will be verified during the build process.

During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, only the top-level declarations and `pkgver()` (if present) are evaluated. This PKGBUILD has no `pkgver()` function, so version remains static. There is no command substitution, external execution, or dynamic fetching in the global scope. The `source` arrays use simple string interpolation with trusted variables (`url`, `pkgver`, `CARCH`) and do not invoke any shell commands or download-and-execute logic.

While the package installs a binary without building from source (as expected for `-bin`), that does not affect the safety of this narrow gate: extraction and checksum verification happen *after* sourcing, and malicious content inside the binary cannot execute under `--nobuild --noprepare`. The actual binary contents will be audited separately later.
</details>
<summary>
No active code execution during source fetch</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- No active code execution during source fetch

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches prebuilt binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 architectures from the project's official GitHub releases page (https://github.com/1ay1/agentty). The sources are versioned and correspond directly to tagged releases (v${pkgver}), which is standard practice for -bin packages. Checksums are provided for both architectures and are expected to be updated by a maintainer script (`release.sh`) prior to release, which explains the placeholder comment — this is a legitimate workflow, not an attempt to bypass verification.

The package installs only a single binary into `/usr/bin` using standard `install` commands, with no additional scripts, patches, or post-install hooks. There are no network operations, file manipulations outside the package directory, or use of dangerous constructs like `eval`, `curl|bash`, or obfuscated code. Dependencies and optdepends are clearly stated and relevant to the application's functionality (e.g., bubblewrap for sandboxing, openssh for airgap feature).

While the package uses prebuilt binaries (inherently less transparent than source-built), the source URLs are pinned to specific release versions over HTTPS, and SHA256 checksums are included. There is no evidence of tampering, backdoors, or supply-chain attacks. The maintainer's workflow involving `release.sh` and `updpkgsums` is normal for automated AUR packaging.
</details>
<summary>
Prebuilt binaries from GitHub; checksums present; no malicious code</summary>

data.reasoning: Both models confirmed PKGBUILD uses pinned GitHub releases with valid checksums, minimal install logic, and no dangerous operations during makepkg execution.
coverage_issues: Both models failed to review .install hooks if present (none existed)
No review of release.sh script mentioned in PKGBUILD comments (though not executed during makepkg)
false_negatives: Potential binary risk: Neither model could audit the prebuilt agentty binary (compiled file)
release.sh script: Mentioned in PKGBUILD but not reviewed; could theoretically tamper with checksums if executed improperly (though not run during makepkg)
learnings: File selection: Prioritize .install scripts when present; treat PKGBUILD-referenced scripts (like release.sh) as secondary review targets
Prompt improvement: Explicitly instruct models to flag PKGBUILD comments referencing external scripts
Failure mode: Improve handling of prebuilt binaries - consider sandboxed execution tests for -bin packages
